newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says Q1 Germany sales down 4.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: VW says Q1 Germany sales down 4.9 percent.

text.p: Volkswagen said its sales during the 1997 first quarter in Germany fell 4.9 percent to 234,000 units over 1996 levels, in part hurt by lost production due to a strike by Spanish truckers.

VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer told the German carmaker's annual news conference that the losses could be made up throughout the year and predicted that VW would show sales growth in Germany for 1997.
Volkswagen said on Thursday it expected the west European vehicle market to show little growth in 1997 amid its prediction for a total market volume of 12.8 million vehicles.
VW said in its annual report released on Thursday that it started the year with 286,000 orders in hand from western Europe, including Germany.

The carmaker expected the United States vehicle market to show some growth to about 9.7 million units for the year but for "serious structural problems" in the Japanese economy to provide only moderate growth to about 4.6 million units.
